rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes Umar reciting the charity, booty, and fayʾ passages, then saying even a shepherd in remote Himyar would receive his share without labor.
rows.anchor: لئن عشت ليأتين الراعي وهو بسرو حمير نصيبه منها لم يعرق فيها جبينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Umar consulted the Muhajirun and Ansar, then concluded that the later-Muslim verse included every Muslim.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه دعا المهاجرين والأنصار واستشارهم فيما فتح الله عليه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar retained the conquered lands of Iraq and Egypt, with their revenues supporting fighters, dependants, and their families; Zubayr, Bilal, and others urged him to distribute them.
rows.anchor: أن عمر أبقى سواد العراق ومصر وما ظهر عليه من الغنائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Umar first sought the army's consent, buying out those who refused; Qurtubi says consensual purchase or relinquishment made this equivalent to the Prophet's division of Khaybar.
rows.anchor: فمن رضي له بترك حظه بغير ثمن ليبقيه للمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other accounts say Umar kept the land without compensating the army, or interpreted the fayʾ verses through the later groups named in 59:8–10.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه أبقاها بغير شيء أعطاه أهل الجيوش

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik allows the imam to hold conquered real estate for the interests of the Muslims.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك: للإمام أن يوقفها لمصالح المسلمين

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa gives the imam a choice between distributing conquered land and holding it for Muslim interests.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة الإمام مخير بين أن يقسمها أو يجعلها وقفا

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says the imam must distribute conquered land unless its owners freely agree to its dedication; those who do not consent retain their property, and Umar obtained consent and bought shares.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: ليس للإمام حبسها عنهم بغير رضاهم، بل يقسمها عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Shafiʿi's view, the verse about later Muslims is detached from the preceding allocation and urges them to pray for and praise their predecessors.
rows.anchor: قلت: وعلى هذا يكون قوله: { والذين جآءوا من بعدهم } مقطوعا مما قبله

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik praised Medina because it was settled through faith and migration, unlike other towns conquered by force, and cited this verse.
rows.anchor: فقال: إن المدينة تبوئت بالإيمان والهجرة، وإن غيرها من القرى افتتحت بالسيف

words: ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the Ansar did not envy the Muhajirun for the fayʾ and other property allotted to them, as commentators generally explain it.
rows.anchor: يعني لا يحسدون المهاجرين على ما خصوا به من مال الفيء وغيره كذلك قال الناس

words: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a host who had only his children's ration, put them to bed and extinguished the lamp to feed a guest; the verse was revealed about this act. Tirmidhi grades the report sound and authentic, and Muslim also records it.
rows.anchor: في الترمذي عن أبي هريرة: أن رجلا بات به ضيف فلم يكن عنده إلا قوته وقوت صبيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction ellipses two nouns: its sense is that they felt no distress at lacking what the Muhajirun received.
rows.anchor: وفيه تقدير حذف مضافين المعنى مس حاجة من فقد ما أوتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything a person feels in the heart that needs to be removed can be called a need or distress.
rows.anchor: وكل ما يجد الإنسان في صدره مما يحتاج إلى إزالته فهو حاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Banu Nadir's property was gained, the Prophet thanked the Ansar for housing and sharing wealth with the Muhajirun, then offered either a joint allotment while they stayed or an allotment to the Muhajirun who would leave.
rows.anchor: إن أحببتم قسمت ما أفاء الله علي من بني النضير بينكم وبينهم

rows.speaker: سعد بن عبادة، سعد بن معاذ
rows.claim: Saʿd ibn ʿUbada and Saʿd ibn Muʿadh chose the fayʾ for the Muhajirun while keeping them in the Ansar's homes; the Ansar consented and the Prophet prayed for mercy upon them and their children.
rows.anchor: فقال سعد بن عبادة وسعد بن معاذ: بل نقسمه بين المهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet gave the Banu Nadir property to the Muhajirun and gave nothing to the Ansar except three men mentioned earlier in the commentary.
rows.anchor: وأعطى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المهاجرين ولم يعط الأنصار شيئا إلا الثلاثة

words: ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse may mean they felt no resentment about what was given even if the amount was small, but remained content with it.
rows.anchor: إذا كان قليلا بل يقنعون به ويرضون عنه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warned the Ansar that they would later see others favored over them and told them to be patient until they met him at the Pool.
rows.anchor: سترون بعدي أثرة فاصبروا حتى تلقوني على الحوض

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In another Abu Hurayra report, the Prophet sought a host for a destitute visitor; an Ansari and his wife pretended to eat while giving the guest their children's food, and God marveled at their act.
rows.anchor: جاء رجل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني مجهود

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A variant names the Ansari host as Abu Talha and says the verse was revealed after the guest was served the household's food.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن أبي هريرة قال:

words: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi attributes the occasion to Thabit ibn Qays staying with Abu al-Mutawakkil, who had only enough food for his children and gave it to his guest.
rows.anchor: وذكر المهدوي عن أبي هريرة أن هذا نزل في ثابت بن قيس

words: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas likewise reports that Thabit ibn Qays was hosted by Abu al-Mutawakkil, who put the children to sleep and served their food to him.
rows.anchor: وكذا ذكر النحاس قال: قال أبو هريرة: نزل برجل من الأنصار يقال له أبو المتوكل

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar's account says a Companion passed a sheep's head to a needier household; it circulated through seven homes and returned to its first recipient, occasioning the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: أهدي لرجل من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأس شاة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi transmits from Anas a similar story: a needy Companion sent a sheep's head through seven households, and it returned to him before the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: ذكره الثعلبي عن أنس قال: أهدى لرجل من الصحابة رأس شاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that on Banu Nadir day the Prophet offered the Ansar a choice: share their homes and wealth with the Muhajirun and share the booty, or keep their property and receive none; they chose to share and prefer the Muhajirun, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم للأنصار يوم بني النضير: «إن شئتم قسمت للمهاجرين من دياركم وأموالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi judges the earlier guest-hosting account of the occasion of revelation more authentic than the preceding alternative account.
rows.anchor: والأول أصح. وفي الصحيحين عن أنس

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, Anas reports that a man had given the Prophet date palms, which the Prophet returned to him after the conquests of Qurayza and Banu Nadir.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أنس: أن الرجل كان يجعل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم النخلات

rows.speaker: الزهري عن أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: The Muhajirun arrived in Medina with nothing; the landowning Ansar shared half their annual fruit and undertook the work and expenses. Umm Sulaym had given the Prophet date palms, which he gave to Umm Ayman.
rows.anchor: لما قدم المهاجرون من مكة إلى المدينة قدموا وليس بأيديهم شيء

words: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithar is preferring another over oneself and worldly interests for religious benefit; it grows from firm certainty, deep love, and patience in hardship. The implied object is the Muhajirun, favored with wealth and homes despite the Ansar's own need.
rows.anchor: الإيثار: هو تقديم الغير على النفس وحظوظها الدنياوية، ورغبة في الحظوظ الدينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb's omitted object is the Muhajirun: the Ansar preferred them in wealth and dwellings despite needing those things themselves.
rows.anchor: ومفعول الإيثار محذوف أي يؤثرونهم على أنفسهم بأموالهم ومنازلهم

words: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة
rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Malik's Muwatta says, in a report reaching him from ʿAʾisha, that she gave her only loaf to a fasting beggar; a sheep wrapped in dough was later gifted to her, and she said that was better than her loaf.
rows.anchor: أنه بلغه عن عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، أن مسكينا سألها وهي صائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars call ʿAʾisha's gift profitable wealth and a virtuous deed whose reward God may hasten without diminishing what is stored; whoever gives something for God will not miss it, and she exemplified the verse.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: هذا من المال الرابح، والفعل الزاكي عند الله تعالى يعجل منه ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'a sheep and its wrapping' refers to a regional delicacy: a slaughtered sheep was covered in wheat dough and baked in a tannur so its drippings stayed in the casing.
rows.anchor: كان هذا من طعامهم، يأتون إلى الشاة أو الخروف إذا سلخوه غطوه كله بعجين البر

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Nafiʿ reports that Ibn ʿUmar repeatedly gave a grape cluster he had bought for a sick person to a beggar, though someone kept buying it back; he would not have eaten it had he known it was the same cluster, since charity should not be taken back.
rows.anchor: وروى النسائي عن نافع أن ابن عمر اشتكى واشتهى عنبا

rows.speaker: مالك الدار
rows.claim: Continuing the report transmitted by Ibn al-Mubarak from Malik al-Dar, Abu Ubayda and Muʿadh each redistributed Umar's 400-dinar gifts among needy households; Umar rejoiced that they were brothers like one another.
rows.anchor: فرجع الغلام إلى عمر، فأخبره فوجده قد أعد مثلها لمعاذ بن جبل

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Qurtubi also mentions that Muʿawiya gave ʿAʾisha ten thousand and that al-Munkadir came in to her.
rows.anchor: ونحوه عن عائشة رضي الله عنها في إعطاء معاوية إياها، وكان عشرة آلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports against giving away all one's property apply to those unlikely to endure poverty and at risk of begging; the Ansar could bear hardship, so giving was better for them, while restraint suits those who cannot endure it.
rows.anchor: إنما كره ذلك في حق من لا يوثق منه الصبر على الفقر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man brought a gold piece as charity, and the Prophet rebuked giving away everything and then sitting to beg from people.
rows.anchor: يأتي أحدكم بجميع ما يملكه فيتصدق به ثم يقعد يتكفف الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving one's life is a higher form of altruism than giving wealth, and Sufi formulations define love as preferring the beloved over oneself; the wife of al-ʿAziz did so for Joseph.
rows.anchor: ومن عبارات الصوفية الرشيقة في حد المحبة: أنها الإيثار، ألا ترى أن امرأة العزيز

rows.speaker: أبو طلحة
rows.claim: The highest self-sacrifice is protecting the Messenger: at Uhud Abu Talha shielded him, begged him not to expose himself, and was struck in his hand while guarding him.
rows.anchor: ففي الصحيح: أن أبا طلحة ترس على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم أحد

rows.speaker: حذيفة العدوي
rows.claim: At Yarmuk, Huthayfa al-ʿAdawi successively offered water to his dying cousin, Hisham ibn al-ʿAs, and another wounded man; each directed the water to the next, and all three died.
rows.anchor: وقال حذيفة العدوي: انطلقت يوم اليرموك أطلب ابن عم لي ومعي شيء من الماء

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
rows.claim: A young man from Balkh told Abu Yazid that true asceticism is gratitude when one has something and preferring others when one has enough; he contrasted this with merely eating when able and enduring hunger otherwise.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد البسطامي: ما غلبني أحد ما غلبني شاب من أهل بلخ

rows.speaker: ذو النون المصري
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nun defined the open-hearted ascetic by three traits: distributing accumulated wealth, not seeking what is absent, and preferring others when food is scarce.
rows.anchor: وسئل ذو النون المصري: ما حد الزاهد المنشرح صدره

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأنطاكي
rows.claim: At a gathering of more than thirty men with too few loaves, they broke the bread, extinguished the lamp, and each left it for the others; afterward none had eaten.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن أبي الحسن الأنطاكي: أنه اجتمع عنده نيف وثلاثون رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khassasa is a need that disrupts one's condition; its root sense is isolation, so it describes being left alone in want.
rows.anchor: الخصاصة: الحاجة التي تختل بها الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses khassasa for scarcity in a line saying spring sustains the sick and enriches the poor when need arises.
rows.anchor: أما الربيع إذا تكون خصاصة عاش السقيم به وأثرى المقتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi initially treats shuhh and bukhl as equivalent terms for miserliness, with forms including shih, shuh, and shuhaha.
rows.anchor: يقال: رجل شحيح بين الشح والشح والشحاحة

rows.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some lexicographers distinguish shuhh from bukhl as the more intense condition.
rows.anchor: وجعل بعض أهل اللغة الشح أشد من البخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Sihah records alternate conjugations of shuhh and its singular and plural forms.
rows.anchor: وشححت أيضا تشح وتشح. ورجل شحيح، وقوم شحاح وأشحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's shuhh includes withholding zakat and non-obligatory duties such as kinship ties and hospitality; spending on these protects one from it, whereas spending lavishly on oneself while neglecting them does not.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالآية: الشح بالزكاة وما ليس بفرض من صلة ذوي الأرحام

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Aswad reports that Ibn Masʿud told a man afraid of his stinginess that Qurʾanic shuhh means unjustly consuming another's wealth, while the man's own condition was bukhl.
rows.anchor: وروى الأسود عن ابن مسعود أن رجلا أتاه فقال له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi underscores Ibn Masʿud's distinction between Qurʾanic shuhh and bukhl.
rows.anchor: ففرق رضي الله عنه بين الشح والبخل

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Tawus says bukhl is withholding one's own property, while shuhh is coveting what other people own by lawful or unlawful means and never being satisfied.
rows.anchor: وقال طاوس: البخل أن يبخل الإنسان بما في يده، والشح أن يشح بما في أيدي الناس

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr defines shuhh as withholding zakat and storing up unlawful wealth.
rows.anchor: ابن جبير: الشح منع الزكاة وادخار الحرام

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna defines shuhh as injustice.
rows.anchor: ابن عيينة: الشح الظلم

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines shuhh as abandoning obligations and violating prohibitions.
rows.anchor: الليث: ترك الفرائض وانتهاك المحارم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas calls one who follows desire and does not accept faith shuhh.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: من اتبع هواه ولم يقبل بالإيمان فذلك الشحيح

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God has protected a person from shuhh if it neither induces him to take what God forbade nor prevents him from giving what God commanded.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: من لم يأخذ شيئا لشيء نهاه الله عنه

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that one is free of shuhh by paying zakat, hosting guests, and giving during hardship.
rows.anchor: وقال أنس: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas also reports the Prophet seeking refuge from the soul's greed, extravagance, and intrusive thoughts.
rows.anchor: وعنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يدعو

rows.speaker: أبو الهياج الأسدي
rows.claim: Abu al-Hayyaj saw ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf asking only to be protected from his own greed; Ibn ʿAwf explained that this protection keeps one from theft, adultery, and similar sins.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الهياج الأسدي: رأيت رجلا في الطواف يدعو: اللهم قني شح نفسي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warned that injustice brings darkness on Judgment Day and that greed destroyed earlier peoples by driving them to bloodshed and violations of sacred limits.
rows.anchor: اتقوا الظلم فإن الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة واتقوا الشح

rows.speaker: كسرى
rows.claim: Chosroes said greed harms people more than poverty: a poor person is satisfied when food appears, while a greedy person is never satisfied.
rows.anchor: وقال كسرى لأصحابه: أي شيء أضر بابن آدم؟ قالوا: الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khaliq here means the one who determines or measures out creation.
rows.anchor: { الخالق } هنا المقدر. و { البارىء } المنشىء المخترع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bariʾ means the initiator who brings things into existence.
rows.anchor: و { البارىء } المنشىء المخترع. و { المصور } مصور الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Musawwir forms images and arranges them in differing configurations; forming is the final stage, following creation and origination.
rows.anchor: و { المصور } مصور الصور ومركبها على هيئات مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forms the human in the womb through three stages: a clot, then a lump, then a recognizable shape and distinguishing appearance.
rows.anchor: جعله علقة، ثم مضغة، ثم جعله صورة وهو التشكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some equate creation with image-making, but Qurtubi rejects this order: determining is first, origination next, and shaping last.
rows.anchor: وقد جعل بعض الناس الخلق بمعنى التصوير، وليس كذلك

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's verse names the creator, originator, and shaper in sequence and describes the stages in the womb.
rows.anchor:
وقال النابغة:
الخالق البارىء المصور في ال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi cites Zuhayr to distinguish executing a plan from merely conceiving it: other people can plan what they cannot successfully carry out.
rows.anchor: يقول: تقدر ما تقدر ثم تفريه، أي تمضيه على وفق تقديرك

rows.speaker: حاطب بن أبي بلتعة
rows.claim: Hatib ibn Abi Baltaʿa read al-bariʾ al-musawwira with the waw vowelled in fatḥa and the ra accusative, meaning the one who brings forth or distinguishes the portrayed forms by their varying configurations; al-Zamakhshari reports it.
rows.anchor: وعن حاطب ابن أبي بلتعة أنه قرأ «البارىء المصور» بفتح الواو ونصب الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse attributes the most beautiful names to God and says everything in heaven and earth glorifies Him; Qurtubi refers readers to his earlier discussion.
rows.anchor: له الأسماء الحسنى يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra asked the Prophet about God's greatest name and was told to recite the end of Surat al-Hashr often; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة قال: سألت خليل أبا القاسم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن اسم الله الأعظم

rows.speaker: جابر بن زيد
rows.claim: Jabir ibn Zayd identifies Allah itself as the greatest name, pointing to this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال جابر بن زيد: إن اسم الله الأعظم هو الله لمكان هذه الآية

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet promising forgiveness of past and future sins to whoever recites Surat al-Hashr; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama reports the Prophet saying that whoever recites the concluding verses of al-Hashr by day or night and dies that day or night is guaranteed Paradise; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: من قرأ خواتم سورة الحشر في ليل أو نهار فقبضه الله في تلك الليلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the ummiyyun are all Arabs, literate or not, because they were not People of Scripture.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الأميون العرب كلهم، من كتب منهم ومن لم يكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view defines the ummiyyun as those who do not write; Quraysh are given as an example.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأميون الذين لايكتبون. وكذلك كانت قريش

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim, as transmitted by Mansur, defines an ummi as one who can read but cannot write.
rows.anchor: وروى منصور عن إبراهيم قال: الأمي الذي يقرأ ولا يكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger sent among them is Muhammad; every Arab tribe had kinship with him and ancestry from him, except Taghlib, whom God kept from his lineage because of their Christianity, according to Ibn Ishaq.
rows.anchor: يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم. وما من حي من العرب إلا ولرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيهم قرابة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Taghlib was excluded from the Prophet's Arab ancestry because of its Christianity, so God did not make them his forebears.
rows.anchor: إلا حي تغلب فإن الله تعالى طهر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم لنصرانيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was unlettered: he had not read from a book or studied one.
rows.anchor: وكان أميا لم يقرأ من كتاب ولم يتعلم

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi gives three reasons an unlettered prophet is a blessing: this matches earlier prophetic glad tidings, resembles the people's circumstances and aids their acceptance, and removes suspicion that he learned revealed books and wisdom by reading.
rows.anchor: قال الماوردي: فإن قيل ما وجه الامتنان فإن بعث نبيا أميا؟ فالجواب عنه من ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says all three reasons demonstrate Muhammad's miracle and the truth of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذا كله دليل معجزته وصدق نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs the Messenger recites to them are the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: { يتلو عليهم آياته } يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains purification as making their hearts pure through faith.
rows.anchor: { ويزكيهم } أي يجعلهم أزكياء القلوب بالإيمان قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن جريج، مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil explain purification as cleansing them of the filth of disbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يطهرهم من دنس الكفر والذنوب قاله ابن جريج ومقاتل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the phrase as the Messenger taking their alms.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: يأخذ زكاة أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book taught by the Messenger is the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: { ويعلمهم الكتاب } يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the wisdom taught by the Messenger as the Sunna.
rows.anchor: { والحكمة } السنة قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the book as writing with a pen, which spread among Arabs through the religious command to record matters in writing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «الكتاب» الخط بالقلم لأن الخط فشا في العرب بالشرع

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik ibn Anas defines wisdom as understanding jurisprudence in religion.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك بن أنس: «الحكمة» الفقه في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Before' means before the Messenger or before he was sent to them.
rows.anchor: أي من قبله وقبل أن يرسل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their manifest error was being far from the truth.
rows.anchor: أي في ذهاب عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being presented before God means facing the reckoning and having deeds laid out for recompense, not informing God of something He did not know; Qurtubi cites 18:48 as a parallel.
rows.anchor: ليس ذلك عرضا يعلم به ما لم يكن عالما به، بل معناه الحساب وتقرير الأعمال عليهم للمجازاة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan transmits from Abu Hurayra that people face three presentations at Resurrection: two for dispute and excuses, then records fly into their hands, right or left. Tirmidhi says it is unsound because al-Hasan did not hear from Abu Hurayra.
rows.anchor: روى الحسن عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: Ibn Shajara explains that God knows every deed, including things people tried to conceal; khafiya means a hidden act.
rows.anchor: ف «خافية» على هذا بمعنى خفية، كانوا يخفونها من أعمالهم قاله ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that no person escapes notice or remains unjudged.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يخفى عليه إنسان أي لا يبقى إنسان لا يحاسب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn ʿAmr says believers will be distinguishable from disbelievers and the righteous from the wicked.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: لا يخفى المؤمن من الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that no nakedness will remain covered, in light of the report that people are resurrected barefoot and naked.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا تستتر منكم عورة

rows.speaker: الكوفيون إلا عاصما
rows.claim: The Kufans except ʿAsim read the verb in the masculine, la yakhfa, because khafiya is grammatically feminine but not feminine in sense; Abu ʿUbayd prefers this reading because the prepositional phrase separates verb and subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون إلا عاصما «لا يخفى» بالياء لأن تأنيث الخافية غير حقيقي

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use the feminine verb, la takhfa; Abu Hatim prefers it because the subject khafiya is feminine.
rows.anchor: الباقون بالتاء. واختاره أبو حاتم لتأنيث الخافية

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Adam was created from the soil of the whole earth; Qurtubi refers to his earlier discussion in al-Anʿam and al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: يعني آدم عليه السلام خلقه من أديم الأرض كلها، قاله ابن جريج

rows.speaker: خالد بن معدان
rows.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan says humans were created from clay and that hearts therefore soften in winter.
rows.anchor: وقال خالد بن معدان: خلق الإنسان من طين، فإنما تلين القلوب في الشتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabatan is a noun placed where the verbal noun would be: the verbal noun of anbata is inbat.
rows.anchor: و«نباتا» مصدر على غير المصدر، لأن مصدره أنبت إنباتا

rows.speaker: الخليل، الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and al-Zajjaj treat nabatan as a verbal noun based on the meaning: God made people grow with a growing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مصدر محمول على المعنى، لأن معنى: «أنبتكم» جعلكم تنبتون نباتا، قاله الخليل والزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading of the syntax is 'He grew plants for you from the earth,' making nabatan an explicit cognate accusative; Qurtubi says the first analysis is clearer.
rows.anchor: فـ«نباتا» على هذا نصب على المصدر الصريح. والأول أظهر

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj also explains that God caused human beings to grow on earth, increasing them from childhood to adulthood and from shortness to height.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: أنبتهم في الأرض بالكبر بعد الصغر وبالطول بعد القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning people to the earth refers to burial when they die.
rows.anchor: { ثم يعيدكم فيها } أي عند موتكم بالدفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing people out of the earth refers to resurrection on the Day of Rising.
rows.anchor: { ويخرجكم إخراجا } بالنشور للبعث يوم القيامة
